title: Live pinned-host verification of the corrected v1.2.0.0 release candidate

matrix.description: The MB/KB byte-unit settings surface: exact byte counts persist as bytes through the elevation-gated save path, and the served settings resource exposes the per-field unit/step/precision mapping and the restart-required note text.
matrix.command: POST Limits.ProviderResponseLimitBytes=1572864, .WebhookMaxPayloadBytes=204800, .InventoryCacheMaxBytes=1048576 through POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration; grep -E '<ProviderResponseLimitBytes>|<WebhookMaxPayloadBytes>|<InventoryCacheMaxBytes>' /tmp/arrtags-21.9/data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml; admin GET .../Configuration; curl -o page21.9.html 'http://127.0.0.1:8096/web/ConfigurationPage?name=ArrTags' and inspect byteLimitFields and the *RestartNote texts
matrix.observed:
SAVE-SIDE BYTE ROUND-TRIP: 'admin GET .../Configuration' -> jq '.Limits.ProviderResponseLimitBytes=1572864 | .Limits.WebhookMaxPayloadBytes=204800 | .Limits.InventoryCacheMaxBytes=1048576' -> POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration -> HTTP 204 with an empty body. The persisted file /tmp/arrtags-21.9/data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml then carries exactly <ProviderResponseLimitBytes>1572864</ProviderResponseLimitBytes>, <WebhookMaxPayloadBytes>204800</WebhookMaxPayloadBytes> and <InventoryCacheMaxBytes>1048576</InventoryCacheMaxBytes> (1.5 MiB, 200 KiB and 1 MiB), and the subsequent administrator GET returns the identical integers {"a":1572864,"b":204800,"c":1048576}. The stored value is therefore the exact byte count and no MB/KB rescaling occurs on the save path. The save applied at runtime with no restart: 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags 1.2.0.0' count and 'Startup complete' count both stayed 1 across the save.
DISPLAY MAPPING IN THE SERVED RESOURCE: GET /web/ConfigurationPage?name=ArrTags (200, 59,154 bytes) contains the byteLimitFields table with one entry per byte-denominated field, each carrying the code-owned unit/step/precision mirroring the C# ByteLimitUnits mapping:
  ProviderResponseLimitBytes unit MB unitBytes 1048576 stepBytes 65536 precision 4
  WebhookMaxPayloadBytes    unit KB unitBytes 1024   stepBytes 1024  precision 0
  SourceArtifactLimitBytes  unit MB unitBytes 1048576 stepBytes 65536 precision 4
  DerivedArtifactLimitBytes unit MB unitBytes 1048576 stepBytes 65536 precision 4
  RenderCacheQuotaBytes     unit MB unitBytes 1048576 stepBytes 1048576 precision 0
  ArtifactStorageQuotaBytes unit MB unitBytes 1048576 stepBytes 1048576 precision 0
  InventoryCacheMaxBytes    unit MB unitBytes 1048576 stepBytes 1048576 precision 0
so the three fields probed above display as 1.5 MB, 200 KB and 1 MB respectively, with per-field step multiples of 0.0625 MB, 1 KB and 1 MB, and with 4, 0 and 0 decimal precision. byteLimitToDisplay renders stored bytes at the field's precision, byteLimitToBytes converts a displayed value back to bytes and rejects a value that is not an exact multiple of the field step with the message 'Enter the value in <unit> as a multiple of <step> <unit>.', and readByteLimitValues feeds the converted bytes back into config.Limits on save.
RESTART-REQUIRED NOTE TEXT: the served resource carries the seven always-present static note elements, three of them the mixed (construction-captured + per-operation) wording and four the simple wording, matching the restartRequiredFields table (SourceArtifactLimitBytes, DerivedArtifactLimitBytes, MaxImageDimensionPixels, RenderCacheTtlMinutes, RenderCacheQuotaBytes, ArtifactStorageQuotaBytes, TerminalProvenanceRetentionDays):
  id="sourceArtifactLimitBytesRestartNote"      -> "A Jellyfin server restart is required for a change to this setting to take effect. Some paths apply the change immediately."
  id="derivedArtifactLimitBytesRestartNote"     -> same mixed text
  id="maxImageDimensionPixelsRestartNote"       -> same mixed text
  id="renderCacheTtlMinutesRestartNote"         -> "A Jellyfin server restart is required for a change to this setting to take effect."
  id="renderCacheQuotaBytesRestartNote"         -> simple text
  id="artifactStorageQuotaBytesRestartNote"     -> simple text
  id="terminalProvenanceRetentionDaysRestartNote" -> simple text
The best-effort modal reminder is also present in the served resource (showRestartRequiredReminder with a Dashboard.alert call, an availability guard and a swallowing try/catch, and the message "A restart-required setting changed. A Jellyfin server restart is required for the change to take effect; the note text next to the setting states whether some paths apply the change immediately.").
LIMITATION (recorded honestly, not a substitute result): the pinned host runs with --nowebclient and the repository has no JavaScript runtime, so the page-side unit conversion, the step-multiple rejection and the modal reminder were verified against the served resource only, not executed live. The server-side byte range check and the byte round-trip were exercised live. This is the same bound already registered as F-21.4-4 / docs/limitations V12-G6-1 and is unchanged by the corrected build.

matrix.description: The read-only diagnostics endpoint is elevation-gated (fail-closed for anonymous), read-only, fixed-shape, bounded and secret-free.
matrix.command: curl -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:8096/ArrTags/Status (anonymous, twice incl. a bogus token); curl -H '<admin>' .../ArrTags/Status | jq; curl -X POST/-X DELETE -H '<admin>' .../ArrTags/Status; curl -w '%{http_code}' -H '<admin>' .../ArrTags/Stats; secret/path regex scan over the body
matrix.observed:
FAIL-CLOSED: anonymous GET /ArrTags/Status -> HTTP 401 with a 0-byte body, and the same 401 with a syntactically valid but wrong MediaBrowser bearer token, so the route rejects unauthenticated and invalidly authenticated callers alike rather than returning a partial snapshot. ADMIN SNAPSHOT: administrator GET /ArrTags/Status -> HTTP 200 with the fixed-shape body {"QueueDepth":0,"QueueInFlight":0,"SonarrHealth":"Healthy","RadarrHealth":"Healthy","MatchingFailures":{"NotFound":4,"Ambiguous":0,"Unsupported":2},"CacheHits":5,"CacheMisses":5,"RenderFailures":{InvalidRequest:0,MalformedSource:0,SourceByteLimitExceeded:0,SourceDimensionLimitExceeded:0,OutputDimensionLimitExceeded:0,OutputByteLimitExceeded:0,ColorPolicyInvalid:0,ContrastTooLow:0,DecodeFailed:0,UnsupportedInput:0,UnsupportedColorProfile:0,FontUnavailable:0,FontInvalid:0,LayoutFailed:0,EncodeFailed:0,NativeAssetUnavailable:0,RenderError:0,Cancelled:0},"StaleMetadataTransitions":0}. SHAPE: 9 top-level fields and 28 leaf scalar paths, which matches the ADR-025 clause 3/4 contract and the 28-entry dashboard panel table. The body contains 0 '[' characters, i.e. no array and no per-item collection; every value is a counter or a bounded enum. The two provider-health fields are the only provider-named strings and are the bounded enum values Healthy/Unavailable/Unknown, not provider URLs, names or credentials. READ-ONLY: administrator POST /ArrTags/Status -> 405, administrator DELETE /ArrTags/Status -> 405, and the sibling route administrator GET /ArrTags/Stats -> 404, so there is no second route and no accepted write verb. SECRET-FREE: a case-insensitive scan of the body for 'radarr|sonarr|/tmp|arrtags|apikey|secret|api.key' returns exactly 2 matches, both the field names RadarrHealth and SonarrHealth; 0 matches for any path, media file, item id, item name, API key, webhook secret or provider payload. The mock API key values and the admin access token do not appear in the body, and neither appears in console.log. LIMITS: the endpoint's own counters are bounded by construction (counters and enums, no free text, no per-item list), so no unbounded value could be returned; the observed body is 0 counters for queue depth and in-flight work because nothing was queued at the sample instant. PANEL RESOURCE: the served settings page contains the static-hidden, empty
under

Diagnostics

with the description 'Read-only process counters for this Jellyfin session. Process-lifetime counters reset when Jellyfin restarts.' The panel ships no data in the resource and holds no credential literal. LIMITATION (not a substitute result): the panel's inline JavaScript is not executed on this --nowebclient host and the repository has no JavaScript runtime, so the panel's own unauthorized behaviour is verified structurally against the endpoint model and the served resource, not by running it; the endpoint-side fail-closed behaviour (401) was observed live. Unchanged from F-21.4-4 and docs/limitations V12-G8-1.

matrix.description: With LogVerbosity=Information, ArrTags log lines identify media by a bounded file name with an item-id fallback, never a directory or full path and never a secret, and the bounded render classification is emitted on the artwork outcome line.
matrix.command: POST LogVerbosity=Information through /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration; grep -oE '\] ArrTags\.[^:]+: .*' /tmp/arrtags-21.9/console.log | sort -u; grep -E '\] ArrTags\.' /tmp/arrtags-21.9/console.log | grep -cE '/tmp/|/media/'; grep -c -E '<radarr key>|<sonarr key>' /tmp/arrtags-21.9/console.log
matrix.observed:
LogVerbosity=Information was set through the elevation-gated POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration (204) and honoured immediately with no restart ('Loaded plugin: ArrTags 1.2.0.0' count 1 and 'Startup complete' count 1 across every save in this run). 65 ArrTags log lines, 28 distinct, all at [INF].
BOUNDED FILE-NAME SUBJECT (ADR-026 clause 1/3) - every media-bearing line identifies the item by its bare file name, never a directory or a full path:
  "Artwork generation for item ArrTags Test Movie (2020).mp4 completed with Published: The derived artwork was published and committed."
  "Artwork generation for item ArrTags Test Show - S01E01.mkv completed with Published: The derived artwork was published and committed."
  "Artwork generation for item ArrTags Sparse Movie (2019).mp4 completed with Published: The derived artwork was published and committed."
  "Artwork generation for item ArrTags Sparse Movie (2019).mp4 completed with RenderPassThrough (PassThroughReason=NoDisplayableValue): The render passed through; the current artwork is preserved."
  "Metadata reconciliation discarded item ArrTags Test Show - S01E01.mkv: The Jellyfin item changed while the work was processing."
BOUNDED RENDER CLASSIFICATION (ADR-026 clause 3) - the parenthesised bounded classification is emitted on the artwork-boundary outcome line, observed as " (PassThroughReason=NoDisplayableValue)" on the pass-through outcome. The Published outcomes carry no classification because the result carries none, exactly as in the task 21.4 run. The classification value is a bounded enum with no free text.
ITEM-ID FALLBACK: the D-format item-identifier fallback ('Metadata reconciliation discarded item <guid>: ...') is the documented alternative at sites where no file name is available. It was not exercised in this run because every media-bearing site had a file name available; the file-name form is the one observed live 5 times here. The fallback is covered by the repository's unit tests and was observed live in the task 21.4 run. Recorded as a scope limit of this row, not as a failure.
SUBJECT-FREE PROVIDER AND COUNTER LINES: "Reconciliation (PostScan|PostSave|Scheduled) Completed: inspected N, eligible N, enqueued N, covered N. The bounded reconciliation reached the end of the candidate order." and "Published metadata state 'Fresh'|'Unmatched' for provider 'radarr'|'sonarr' at configuration vN." and "Suppressed N repeated 'MetadataPublished' ArrTags log messages." - the suppression counters show the log volume is bounded rather than proportional to work.
PATH AND SECRET EXCLUSION: ArrTags log lines containing a directory or media path ('/tmp/' or '/media/') = 0. Occurrences of the mock Radarr API key = 0, of the mock Sonarr API key = 0, of the configured webhook secret = 0. The mock fixture server's own request log likewise never prints a key value (it logs apiKey=valid / apiKey=missing-unenforced only), and that log was inspected as well.
LENGTH BOUND: the longest ArrTags log line prefix measured 118 characters, far under the documented 128-scalar subject bound; no unbounded or machine-generated subject was observed.
CONFIGURED VERBOSITY HONOURED (extra evidence): POST LogVerbosity=Off -> 204, then a scheduled-task trigger produced 0 new ArrTags log lines; POST LogVerbosity=Warning -> 204, then a trigger produced 0 new ArrTags [INF] lines; POST LogVerbosity=Information -> 204 restored the Information stream. All three transitions applied at runtime with no restart.

matrix.description: A simultaneous outage of both providers leaves the host up, leaves every published image byte-unchanged, and emits only bounded provider-unavailable warnings with no fatal error; clearing the outage restores provider health.
matrix.command: touch 21.9fix/radarr/failure 21.9fix/sonarr/failure; curl -H "X-Api-Key: $RADARRKEY" http://127.0.0.1:7978/api/v3/system/status; curl -X POST -H '<admin>' http://127.0.0.1:8096/ScheduledTasks/Running/0e96fc3004bcd22db45dd641e63e2666; GET /System/Info/Public; GET /Items/{id}/Images/Primary vs the pre-outage baseline; then rm -f the markers, re-verify 200, re-trigger and confirm health returns to Healthy
matrix.observed:
OUTAGE INJECTION (the documented marker mechanism, applied to the verifier's own fixture copy so no committed file is touched): 'touch 21.9fix/radarr/failure 21.9fix/sonarr/failure' after capturing the pre-outage served bytes for all three items. The outage was confirmed at the source: with the mock Radarr key, GET http://127.0.0.1:7978/api/v3/system/status -> 503 and /api/v3/movie -> 503; with the mock Sonarr key, GET http://127.0.0.1:9089/api/v3/system/status -> 503 and /api/v3/series -> 503. The mock server itself stayed up and logged 31 status=503 responses during the window.
TRIGGER: 'POST /ScheduledTasks/Running/0e96fc3004bcd22db45dd641e63e2666' -> HTTP 204 at 2026-09-29T15:24:35Z. No library refresh was used, so no sidecar re-adoption occurred during this row.
HOST STAYS UP: GET /System/Info/Public returned HTTP 200 both while the providers were 503 and after the outage run.
ARTWORK UNCHANGED: 'cmp' of the post-outage served bytes against the pre-outage baseline is identical for all three items - EP 20,311 bytes b57d0cde...a9ef, sparse movie 17,270 bytes 49e477e5...6cab, test movie 17,839 bytes 9b31a65c...0b73 - and each still equals its persisted ActiveImageIdentity. The persisted artwork-state files were not rewritten (no new publication, no identity change).
BOUNDED WARNINGS: exactly 15 new console lines for the whole outage window, of which 13 are ArrTags [WRN] and every one of them is a provider-unavailable message: 7 "Provider read failed for connection 'radarr:http://127.0.0.1:7978'|'sonarr:http://127.0.0.1:9089' (radarr|sonarr): ProviderUnavailable (Later). The provider returned a server error." and 6 "Metadata read failed for item ArrTags Test Movie (2020).mp4 | ArrTags Sparse Movie (2019).mp4 | ArrTags Test Show - S01E01.mkv (radarr|sonarr): ProviderUnavailable (Later). The provider returned a server error.", plus 2 host-level [INF] lines (the scheduled-task completion and the reconciliation summary 'inspected 3, eligible 3, enqueued 3, covered 3'). The log volume is therefore bounded and not proportional to the 31 503 responses the mock served. Subjects are bounded file names or connection ids, never a path: new lines matching '/tmp/' or '/media/' = 0.
ERROR COUNTS: [FTL] 0 across the whole run; ArrTags-logger [ERR] 0 across the whole run. (The single [ERR] in the run is the pre-existing host-internal CollectionFolderMetadataService collection-folder collage condition, unrelated to ArrTags - see F-21.9-3.)

findings.detail: docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md now records the OwnershipLost caution and the working trigger (complete library/sidecar setup and the final full refresh before the first publication; use POST /ScheduledTasks/Running/<ArrTags task id> afterwards), which was F-21.4-5's recommendation. Two smaller gaps remain. (1) The 'v1.2 procedure' text still says to configure the plugin by hand-writing PREFIX/data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml in the base task 7.3 reproduction, and the v1.1/v1.2 additions only imply the elevation-gated path; the v1.2 release requires configuration only through POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration, and a verifier following the older step literally would not exercise the shipped path. (2) The procedure does not say that after a provider-fixture edit the verifier must issue one configuration save before expecting the scheduled reconciliation task to cover the change. The scheduled run resumes from the persisted ADR-022 durable reconciliation cursor anchor and covers the library round-robin across successive runs, so it is not guaranteed to re-cover the edited item, while the post-save trigger is deliberately excluded from the cursor and always enumerates from the start (ADR-022 clause 6). A verifier who edits a provider fixture and only runs the scheduled task can therefore see the changed record remain unpublished and wrongly conclude that changed metadata does not republish. This is not provider-inventory-cache staleness: every reconciliation, including the scheduled one, discards the retained observation sets unconditionally (ADR-018 clause 3; LibraryReconciliationService.ReconcileAsync calls InvalidateInventory()). Both were hit in this run and worked around without touching the product.
evidence: docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md 'Reproduction of the task 7.3 end-to-end run' step 2: 'Configure the plugin by writing PREFIX/data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml ... and restart the host; runtime configuration replacement is a documented Phase 7 deferral, so a restart is the supported mechanism.' - superseded for v1.2 by the elevation-gated path.

In this run, after editing the verifier's own radarr/moviefile.json to give the sparse movie a file record, the scheduled task at 15:20:23Z did not re-render the sparse item (it still produced 'RenderPassThrough (PassThroughReason=NoDisplayableValue)'), and the change only became visible after an additional configuration save (the post-save trigger) at 15:21:40Z, which published the sparse item. The scheduled run cannot have served a cached pre-edit provider observation: every reconciliation discards the retained observation sets unconditionally (src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/LibraryReconciliationService.cs:139 calls InvalidateInventory(), ADR-018 clause 3), asserted for PostScan, Scheduled and PostSave by tests/ArrTags.Tests/ReconciliationTriggerTests.cs:254 (ReconciliationInvalidatesTheInventoryForEverySource). The consistent explanation is the ADR-022 durable reconciliation cursor, which governs only scheduled and post-scan runs (LibraryReconciliationService.cs:151 sets usesCursor for Scheduled or PostScan): a scheduled run resumes from the persisted anchor and covers the library round-robin across successive runs, while the post-save trigger always enumerates from the start and leaves the cursor untouched (docs/decisions/ADR-022.md:105-113, clause 6).

docs/implementation/14.3/live-verification.json records for the v1.1 run that every reconciliation discards the retained observation sets (LibraryReconciliationService.InvalidateInventory) and that the post-save and library-refresh windows each produced fresh provider reads, i.e. per-reconciliation invalidation, not a save needed to refresh a stale inventory cache.
findings.recommended_action: In the v1.2 section of docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md, state that the plugin must be configured only through POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration (never by hand-editing ArrTags.xml) and that after editing a provider fixture the verifier must issue one configuration save, whose post-save reconciliation always enumerates from the start and therefore covers the change, because a scheduled run resumes from the persisted ADR-022 cursor anchor and only covers the library round-robin across successive runs. Do not attribute the need for the save to provider-inventory-cache staleness: every reconciliation, including a scheduled one, invalidates the inventory (ADR-018 clause 3).
findings.correction: R-21.9-1 (MEDIUM, attempt-2 rework): the original F-21.9-6 detail and evidence attributed the post-fixture-edit stale observation to the provider inventory cache still serving the pre-edit read. The implementation contradicts that mechanism - LibraryReconciliationService.ReconcileAsync calls InvalidateInventory() unconditionally at the top of every run (src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/LibraryReconciliationService.cs:139), and ReconciliationInvalidatesTheInventoryForEverySource asserts PostScan, Scheduled and PostSave each discard the retained observation sets (tests/ArrTags.Tests/ReconciliationTriggerTests.cs:254) - so the causal attribution was corrected to the ADR-022 durable reconciliation cursor (scheduled/post-scan resume from the persisted anchor and cover the library round-robin; the post-save trigger always enumerates from the start). The underlying observation and the practical procedure instruction (issue one configuration save after a fixture edit) are unchanged.

notes: SCOPE. This is the Phase 21 corrective re-run of the v1.2 pinned-host end-to-end matrix against the corrected 1.2.0.0 release candidate produced by task 21.8 (SEC-21.5-01 transport fix). Changed provider metadata did republish: adding a movie-file record for the sparse movie produced a fresh 'Published: The derived artwork was published and committed.' with a new ActiveImageIdentity. The sparse movie was not re-rendered by the scheduled run after the edit; establishing the change required one configuration save, because the post-save trigger always enumerates from the start while the scheduled run resumes from the persisted ADR-022 cursor anchor and covers the library round-robin across successive runs (every reconciliation, including the scheduled one, already invalidates the provider inventory, ADR-018 clause 3) - see F-21.9-6.
